subject: kmer-polynomials manuscript: strand-symmetric hash claim (FULL tier: no round has ruled on any claim in this paper)

claims.text: [the user's claim] (F+λ)(R+λ) over F_q with the Eisenstein encoding is injective on double-stranded k-mers with a provable ~2k/q collision bound, and the obvious shortcuts F+R and F·R are degenerate. Refuted if the unique-factorization step does not show S(s)−S(u) is a NONZERO polynomial for every pair of distinct double-stranded classes, if 'injective' overstates a probabilistic statement, if the total-degree bound 2(k−1) or the 2.7×10⁻¹⁷ arithmetic is wrong, if independence of x, λ from the input is insufficiently stated, or if the exhaustive k=7/8 checks (results/kp7_symmetric_check_2026-11-10.txt, results/kp7_eisenstein_2026-11-10.md) do not reproduce or do not test what they claim. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Its unique factorization in $\lambda$ separates distinct double-stranded k-mers

claims.text: [mathematical] F+R depends only on mirror differences and takes at most 9^⌊k/2⌋ values (729 at k=7, 6,561 at k=8); F·R cannot tell a k-mer from its plain reverse (4,160 and 16,362 values). Refuted if the formulas are wrong, the counts do not reproduce, or the table caption's encoding/field (fourth-root, q=2^31−1) is not what produced them. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: The sum $F + R = \sum_t s_t (x^t - x^{k-1-t})$ depends only on the mirror differences

claims.text: [mathematical] Rolling rules F_{j+1}=(F_j−s_j)x⁻¹+s_{j+k}x^{k−1} and R_{j+1}=x(R_j+s_j x^{k−1})−s_{j+k} are correct for F=p(x), R=−x^{k−1}p(1/x); single-strand bound (k−1)/q. Refuted if either recurrence is wrong. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

[field facts] q=2^61−1 ≡ 1 (mod 3) so a primitive cube root ω lies in F_q; q ≡ 3 (mod 4) so i does not, and the fourth-root hash lives in F_{q²} at about twice the multiplications. Refuted if a congruence is wrong or the cost ratio is not ~2 (47.37 vs 24.69 cycles in results/paper_bench_2026-11-11.md). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Because $q \equiv 1 \pmod 3$, a primitive cube root of unity exists in $\mathbb{F}_q$

claims.text: [priority / definitional] The criterion: with complement as negation, transitions separate from A–C/G–T transversions exactly when Re(A C̄)≠0; no fourth-root map satisfies it; it is presented as this paper's contribution ('narrower'). Refuted if the identity or the 'exactly when' is wrong, if some fourth-root map does satisfy it, or if the criterion is already published (an absence/priority claim: the paper carries NO dated search marker for it). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Our contribution here is narrower, the criterion for complex maps in which complement is negation.

claims.text: [priority, no number] 'We contribute four things': the second contribution, using these values as polynomial hash coefficients over F_q with a strand-symmetric product whose bound holds for every input, is implied new. Refuted if a strand-symmetric polynomial/product hash with a proven bound (or (F+λ)(R+λ) itself, or a symmetric-polynomial canonical hash) is already published; the paper cites no dated search for this absence. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Second, the use of these values as polynomial hash coefficients over $\mathbb{F}_q$, with a strand-symmetric product whose collision bound holds for every input.

claims.text: [attribution / provenance] Cristea 2002 already made complement a negation via the fourth-root map (up to global sign) and the θ=π/4 trigonometric point; Das, Nanda and Das 2017 fixed θ=π/3, our map up to rotation; their rationale restates Cristea's, mentions no distances, asserts the angle; printed sensitivity is the value of their specificity formula; text and two tables give three exon ranges; Anastassiou makes complement a conjugation; Mendizabal's Table 6 shows spectra cannot tell strand from complement. Refuted if any of these readings of the sources is wrong (check the library summaries AND the PDFs). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Das, Nanda and Das fixed the family's angle at $\theta = \pi/3$

claims.text: [mathematical] With A=1, C=ω: squared distances 1 (transitions), 3 (A–C, G–T transversions), 4 (complements); the field hash keeps the algebra, not the distances. Refuted if the arithmetic is wrong or the sentence implies the hash measures substitution distance. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: so the squared distances are 1 for transitions, 3 for the A–C and G–T transversions, and 4 for complements

claims.text: [empirical] In pairwise alignments of cannabis assemblies on NC_044378.1, 61–65% of substitutions are transitions (Ts/Tv 1.58–1.85). Refuted if the source (results/ideas_eisenstein_2026-11-10.md, ideas/eisenstein/kp1_tstv.py) does not give these, if 61–65% does not follow from 1.58–1.85, or if the alignment set is mis-described. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: 61 to 65 percent of substitutions are transitions (Ts/Tv 1.58 to 1.85)

claims.text: [speed] Every timing comes from one laila job (08653d9e6a7453a2), two interleaved repeats ≤1.3% apart, load cost subtracted: Eisenstein every k-mer 24.69 cycles = 0.46× batched ntHash (11.37); library interface 23.53; fourth-root 47.37; AVX2 26.43; AVX-512 25.86; the Eisenstein scalar code 'matches the 16-lane AVX-512 code'. Refuted if the raw counters (results/paper_bench_2026-11-11/) do not give these, if the comparison is unfair (flags, input, the batched baseline not bit-identical to the library), or if two repeats cannot support the precision quoted. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: the hash costs 24.7 cycles per k-mer on every k-mer, 0.46 times the speed of a batched ntHash

claims.text: [speed, extrapolated] A kept k-mer costs about 28.5 cycles, so the sampler is faster than batched ntHash at sampling rates of 1/20 and below. Refuted if 1/20 is not supported by measurement (the table measures 1/16 at 0.97× and 1/100 at 1.14×; 1/20 is interpolated from a slope between rows using DIFFERENT evaluation modes), or if 'and below' fails anywhere in the range. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: a sampler that computes it only for kept k-mers is faster than batched ntHash at sampling rates of 1/20 and below

claims.text: [equivalence] The batched ntHash reimplementation reproduces the library's hashes bit for bit and runs about twice as fast as the library's per-k-mer interface. Refuted if the bit-for-bit check is absent, partial (e.g. only some k-mers or only canonical values), or if 'about twice' is wrong. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: The baseline is a batched reimplementation of ntHash's canonical roll that reproduces the library's hashes bit for bit

claims.text: [sampling quality] Across cs10 and five seeds, minimizer density within 0.4% of 2/(w+1) at w=10,20,50 for four methods; max per-bit deviation 0.0009–0.0010 (Eisenstein 0.00090 vs ntHash 0.00088); tens of threshold-sampling gaps >200 k-mers per seed vs 0.14 expected; all but 2 of 1,774 in soft-masked repeats, none of the Eisenstein hash's 367 outside. Refuted if the numbers do not reproduce from results/kp7_stats_seeds_eisenstein_2026-11-11.md and its TSVs, if 0.14 is mis-derived, or if 'so the long gaps reflect repeats' does not follow (47.7% of cs10 is soft-masked). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: All but 2 of the 1,774 such gaps lay in soft-masked repeats

claims.text: [spaced seeds] (F_m+λ)(R_m+λ) is strand-symmetric for any 0/1 mask; ntHash2 warns its reverse-complement hashing becomes inconsistent for non-palindromic masks; at 1% substitutions our hash kept 0.747 of windows unchanged (the exact double-stranded value) vs 0.818 for ntHash2; 0.76× ntHash2 speed. Refuted if a non-palindromic mask breaks symmetry (the mirror of a mask is applied to R?), if ntHash2 does not so warn, or if the 0.818 > 0.747 comparison is misread (a HIGHER unchanged fraction from ntHash2 is presented as inconsistency, not as better). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Because $(F_m + \lambda)(R_m + \lambda)$ is strand-symmetric for any mask

claims.text: [set sketch] Power-sum sketch: 11.3 bytes per difference on Cannbio-2 vs GigaDB (3,238,101 differences), exact in every run; km-peeler k-mer table 20.5 bytes at 1.05× in 30/30 (15/30 at 1.0×, tested on 4 of 64 partitions); extended syncmers 4.2 bytes, 1,986,807 spurious, 7 missed, 61% spurious, 2.7× smaller; 0.55× / 1.8× the bytes of an IBLT 'of equal reliability'. Refuted if the numbers do not reproduce from results/kp10_vs_shibuya_2026-11-11*, if 'equal reliability' compares unequal regimes (4 of 64 partitions, 30 trials vs deterministic), or if the bytes accounting differs between methods. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: it needed 11.3 bytes per difference, against 20.5 for an invertible Bloom lookup table of equal reliability

claims.text: [set sketch, no number] The c extra sums make overflow detection deterministic: 'a bucket holding more than m differences is detected rather than resolved wrongly'; the Discussion says the sketch 'detected its own overflow deterministically'. Refuted if a bucket with >m differences can produce m+c power sums consistent with a ≤m solution (then detection is probabilistic over the hash, not deterministic). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: so a bucket holding more than $m$ differences is detected rather than resolved wrongly

claims.text: [orientation] Between Cannbio-2 and its draft, the sketch recovered all 7,931 differences in 137 KB in one round, where km-peeler's extended-syncmer method saw 48,293,748 differences because the draft's contigs lie in other orientations; a canonical k-mer table is orientation-blind too, so the advantage holds against the extended-syncmer method only. Refuted if the 48M is not caused by orientation, if 137 KB is mis-computed, or if the abstract/introduction ('a strand-specific method saw 48 million') overstate what the Discussion concedes. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: where a strand-specific method saw 48 million

claims.text: [comparison framing, no number] ntHash and ntHash2 'fix their seeds, so their collision behaviour is measured, not proven'; ntHash2's sum of strand hashes was exact on all double-stranded 8-mers 'only in our test'; constant-time rolling, substitution and concatenation hold for ntHash too, which is linear over GF(2). Refuted if ntHash's seeds are not fixed, if ntHash/ntHash2 have a proven collision bound, if ntHash is not GF(2)-linear (it uses rotations and XOR plus a final multiply/mix?), or if the 8-mer test does not exist. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Both fix their seeds, so a collision in one run occurs in every run, and their quality is established by measurement.

claims.text: [literature reading] Marçais and colleagues show that canonicalization negates the window guarantee of syncmer-style schemes but has no visible effect on fractional sampling. Refuted if the reading of marcais_2024_knonical is wrong (library summary and PDF). Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Marçais and colleagues show that folding a k-mer with its reverse complement negates the window guarantee of syncmer-style schemes

claims.text: [testing] Every variant checked against the reference roller over windows with N, block sizes 1–4,096, both strands; deliberately broken versions fail; every sketch recovery compared element by element; the Padé negative-index bug showed only as extra rounds (3 instead of 1) and one-sided tests fail without the fix. Refuted if the tests in hash/ and tests/ do not do this, or the mutants do not fail. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: Deliberately broken versions (a wrong sign on the incoming base, a shifted lane remainder, $\lambda$ missing from the table) must fail these tests, and they do.

claims.text: [supplement] De Bruijn adjacency exact on 13.6M edges, 4–6× slower; DFT bound pruned 21% vs 77% possible; FFT diagonals 97–99% precision, <2/3 of aligned bases; 7,760 palindromic 20-mers; haplotypes differ in 42% of chromosome 7 31-mers; Z_4^k transform 1,370× faster at k=12, d=3 and 'probably known'. Refuted if any number does not reproduce from results/ideas_*.md, or if a 'did not pay off' verdict does not follow. Evidence map: manuscript/ledger.md.

source.quote: 1,370 times faster than direct enumeration at $k = 12$, $d = 3$
